gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: They ___ married in a small ceremony in 2011.
gaps.explanation: A dated single event takes the past simple: got.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ at six tomorrow morning, as it does every day.
gaps.explanation: Timetabled events use the present simple.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the same bus to work every morning, even in winter.
gaps.hint: every morning signals a fixed routine
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' describes a fixed routine, which takes the present simple: catches.

gaps.sentence: There ___ a cinema on this corner, but it closed years ago.
gaps.hint: a past state that has ended
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' is also used for past states that no longer exist: used to be.
